items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Gini coefficient"?
options: An adjustment of income figures to account for differences in the cost of living between countries
The line on a 1980 map dividing the richer "North" from the poorer "South", from the Brandt Report
A measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 or 100 (one person has all income)
Aid that must be spent on goods or services from the donor country
items.answer: A measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 or 100 (one person has all income)
items.markingKey: C. "Gini coefficient" is a measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 or 100 (one person has all income).

items.stem: Briefly explain why PPP adjustments are used to compare incomes.
items.answer: Prices differ between countries, so a dollar buys more in India than in the USA; PPP shows what incomes can actually buy.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Prices differ between countries, so a dollar buys more in India than in the USA; PPP shows what incomes can actually buy. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between HDI and GDP per capita.
items.answer: GDP per capita measures average economic output; HDI is a composite of health, education and income.
items.markingKey: GDP per capita measures average economic output; HDI is a composite of health, education and income. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Outline one way in which Kerala, India shows social development with moderate income.
items.answer: Kerala has had much higher literacy and life expectancy than India's average despite a similar or modest income level, due to long-term public investment in health and education. It shows that high human development is possible without very high GDP per capita.
items.markingKey: Context (Kerala has had much higher literacy and life expectancy than India's average despite a similar or modest income level, due to long-term public investment in health and education.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: it shows that high human development is possible without very high GDP per capita. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to social development with moderate income.

items.stem: Approximate UNDP data for Norway (2022): life expectancy 83.2 years, expected years of schooling 18.6, mean years of schooling 13.1, GNI per capita (PPP) US$ 69,200. Using: health index = (LE − 20) ÷ 65; education index = (EYS ÷ 18 + MYS ÷ 15) ÷ 2; income index = (ln GNI − ln 100) ÷ (ln 75 000 − ln 100); HDI = cube root of (health × education × income), calculate the HDI to 3 decimal places.
items.markingKey: Health 0.972 (A1); education 0.937 (A1); income 0.988 (A1); HDI = (0.972 × 0.937 × 0.988)^(1/3) = 0.965 (M1 A1). Small differences from published HDI come from rounding and data revisions.

items.stem: Evaluate the research question "Which country is the most developed?" for an MYP Individuals and Societies investigation into measuring development: GDP per capita, the HDI and other indicators. Rewrite it so that it is clear, focused and researchable.
items.answer: Weakness: it is a closed question Improved: "How far does Kerala's experience show that public spending on health and education can raise human development without high income?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is a closed question); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How far does Kerala's experience show that public spending on health and education can raise human development without high income?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Amartya Sen, Development as Freedom, Oxford, 1999

The author argued that development should be seen as a process of expanding the real freedoms that people enjoy, such as freedom from hunger, disease and illiteracy, and political freedom, rather than only as growth in income.

With reference to its origin and purpose, analyse the value and limitations of Source A for a student investigating measuring development: GDP per capita, the HDI and other indicators.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Amartya Sen, Development as Freedom, Oxford, 1999. Purpose: to propose a broader understanding of development. Value: It is an influential work by a Nobel laureate that shaped the HDI. Limitation: It is a philosophical framework; freedoms are harder to measure than income.
items.markingKey: Origin: Paraphrase of Amartya Sen, Development as Freedom, Oxford, 1999. Purpose: to propose a broader understanding of development. Value: It is an influential work by a Nobel laureate that shaped the HDI. Limitation: It is a philosophical framework; freedoms are harder to measure than income. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". MYP I&S criterion D (year 5), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly discusses concepts, issues, models and theories, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, effectively analyses and evaluates a wide range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and thoroughly interprets a range of perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate; 1-2 limited.

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "How far does Kerala's experience show that public spending on health and education can raise human development without high income?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Use NFHS and HDI data, state budget data and two studies; compare with other states; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Use NFHS and HDI data, state budget data and two studies; compare with other states; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the HDI is considered a better measure of development than GDP per capita alone.
items.answer: It combines income with health and education, reflecting the idea that development is about expanding people's capabilities, not just income.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It combines income with health and education, reflecting the idea that development is about expanding people's capabilities, not just income. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "A high GDP per capita means everyone in a country is well off." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It is an average; high inequality, as in some oil-rich states, can leave many people poor.
items.markingKey: It is an average; high inequality, as in some oil-rich states, can leave many people poor. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which of the following is the most clear and focused research question for an investigation into measuring development: GDP per capita, the HDI and other indicators?
options: Which country is the most developed?
How far does Kerala's experience show that public spending on health and education can raise human development without high income?
items.answer: How far does Kerala's experience show that public spending on health and education can raise human development without high income?
items.markingKey: D. It is open, has a clear scope (place/period/group) and can be answered with evidence; the others are too broad, closed or off-topic.

items.stem: Income shares (World Bank estimates): the United States – poorest 20% 5.2%, richest 20% 47.0%; Japan – poorest 20% 7.5%, richest 20% 39.8%. Calculate the 20:20 ratio for each country and explain why measures of inequality are needed alongside GDP per capita.
items.answer: the United States: 9.0; Japan: 5.3
items.markingKey: the United States 9.0 (A1); Japan 5.3 (A1); comparison (A1). Explanation (2): averages hide how income is distributed; two countries with similar GDP per capita can have very different poverty levels.

items.stem: Which World Bank group includes India as of 2024?
items.answer: Lower-middle income
items.markingKey: D. GNI per capita about US$ 2,500.

items.stem: A student claims: "All countries in the Global South are poor." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The South includes rich economies such as Singapore and Qatar and large emerging economies such as China and Brazil.
items.markingKey: The South includes rich economies such as Singapore and Qatar and large emerging economies such as China and Brazil. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between the development gap within countries and the development gap between countries.
items.answer: Between countries it compares national averages; within countries it compares regions, cities and rural areas or social groups.
items.markingKey: Between countries it compares national averages; within countries it compares regions, cities and rural areas or social groups. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why there are large development differences within countries.
items.answer: Investment, jobs and services often concentrate in cities and core regions, while rural and peripheral areas lag behind, as between Maharashtra and Bihar in India.
items.markingKey: Content: Investment, jobs and services often concentrate in cities and core regions, while rural and peripheral areas lag behind, as between Maharashtra and Bihar in India. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Amara argues that "The Brandt line is no longer useful for understanding global development." Priya disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests.
items.markingKey: Amara: NICs and emerging economies have blurred the divide. Priya: it still captures a broad historical and power divide in global institutions. Judgement (1-2 marks): The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "The Brandt line is no longer useful for understanding global development."
items.answer: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: NICs and emerging economies have blurred the divide; income groups and HDI give more nuance. Arguments against: it still captures a broad historical and power divide in global institutions; many "South" countries share colonial histories and interests. Supported judgement: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "World Bank income groups"?
options: The total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year divided by its population
The UN target, agreed in 1970, for rich countries to give 0.7% of gross national income as aid
The classification of countries as low, lower-middle, upper-middle or high income by GNI per capita
The line on a 1980 map dividing the richer "North" from the poorer "South", from the Brandt Report
items.answer: The classification of countries as low, lower-middle, upper-middle or high income by GNI per capita
items.markingKey: C. "World Bank income groups" is the classification of countries as low, lower-middle, upper-middle or high income by GNI per capita.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the development gap has widened for some countries.
items.answer: Conflict, debt, commodity dependence, weak governance and climate shocks have held back some low-income countries while others grew quickly.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Conflict, debt, commodity dependence, weak governance and climate shocks have held back some low-income countries while others grew quickly. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "How has the development gap between South Korea and Ghana changed since 1960, and why?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Use World Bank and Penn World Table data, two studies on policy; graph GDP per capita; evaluate explanations; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Use World Bank and Penn World Table data, two studies on policy; graph GDP per capita; evaluate explanations; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem:
Source A – Commission report (paraphrased): Paraphrase of the Independent Commission on International Development Issues (chair Willy Brandt), North–South: A Programme for Survival, 1980

The report argued that the North and the South had a mutual interest in reducing poverty and inequality: a more prosperous South would provide markets and stability for the North. It called for large transfers of resources, reform of international institutions and an end to protectionism.

"The Brandt line is no longer useful for understanding global development." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?
items.answer: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests.
items.markingKey: From the source: North and South share an interest in reducing global inequality. Own knowledge for: NICs and emerging economies have blurred the divide; income groups and HDI give more nuance. Own knowledge against: it still captures a broad historical and power divide in global institutions; many "South" countries share colonial histories and interests. Judgement: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 5), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly discusses concepts, issues, models and theories, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, effectively analyses and evaluates a wide range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and thoroughly interprets a range of perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate; 1-2 limited.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The theory that poorer countries remain underdeveloped because of exploitative economic relationships with richer countries"?
items.answer: dependency theory
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of dependency theory.

items.stem: Priya writes: "Natural resources always make a country rich." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The resource curse shows that oil or minerals can encourage corruption, conflict and dependence.
items.markingKey: The resource curse shows that oil or minerals can encourage corruption, conflict and dependence. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between physical causes of uneven development and human causes.
items.answer: Physical causes include climate, disease, hazards and relief; human causes include history, trade, debt, governance and conflict.
items.markingKey: Physical causes include climate, disease, hazards and relief; human causes include history, trade, debt, governance and conflict. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Formulate an action plan to investigate the research question "How far does governance explain the different development paths of Botswana and Zimbabwe since 1980?" Include the main steps, at least one primary and one secondary source, and how you would record your findings.
items.answer: Use World Bank data, corruption indices and two studies; compare factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Use World Bank data, corruption indices and two studies; compare factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Using accurate subject terminology and at least one specific example, write a structured paragraph that responds to: Explain why being landlocked can slow development.
items.answer: Exports and imports must cross other countries, raising transport costs and delays and making trade dependent on neighbours' infrastructure and politics.
items.markingKey: Content: Exports and imports must cross other countries, raising transport costs and delays and making trade dependent on neighbours' infrastructure and politics. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "Historical factors such as colonialism are the most important cause of uneven development today."
items.answer: Colonial history shaped starting conditions, but post-independence choices, institutions and global economics explain much of today's variation.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: colonial economic structures and borders persist; dependency on commodity exports continues. Arguments against: many former colonies such as South Korea and Singapore developed rapidly; governance, conflict and policy since independence matter greatly. Supported judgement: Colonial history shaped starting conditions, but post-independence choices, institutions and global economics explain much of today's variation.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Rostow's model"?
options: An index measuring poverty through deprivations in health, education and living standards
The classification of countries as low, lower-middle, upper-middle or high income by GNI per capita
Terms for generally high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries
W. W. Rostow's 1960 model of five stages of economic growth, from traditional society to high mass consumption
items.answer: W. W. Rostow's 1960 model of five stages of economic growth, from traditional society to high mass consumption
items.markingKey: D. "Rostow's model" is W. W. Rostow's 1960 model of five stages of economic growth, from traditional society to high mass consumption.

items.stem: Explain why "How far does governance explain the different development paths of Botswana and Zimbabwe since 1980?" is a suitable research question for an MYP investigation into the causes of uneven development: physical, historical, economic and political factors.
items.answer: It compares two neighbouring countries to test explanations.
items.markingKey: It compares two neighbouring countries to test explanations. Award marks for relevance to the unit's concepts or global context, and for showing the question is focused and can be answered with available sources. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: With reference to Botswana's diamonds, explain how it illustrates good governance and resources.
items.answer: After diamonds were discovered in 1967, Botswana used revenues for education, health and infrastructure, with low corruption; it became upper-middle income. Institutions made the difference in avoiding the resource curse.
items.markingKey: Context (After diamonds were discovered in 1967, Botswana used revenues for education, health and infrastructure, with low corruption; it became upper-middle income.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: institutions made the difference in avoiding the resource curse. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to good governance and resources.

items.stem: Which 1996 initiative by the IMF and World Bank aimed to reduce the debts of the poorest countries?
items.answer: The Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) Initiative
items.markingKey: The Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) Initiative. 37 countries have received relief.

items.stem: Briefly explain why debt relief can help development.
items.answer: Money spent on debt repayments can be redirected to health, education and infrastructure; Tanzania used savings to abolish primary school fees in 2001.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Money spent on debt repayments can be redirected to health, education and infrastructure; Tanzania used savings to abolish primary school fees in 2001. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between long-term development aid and emergency aid.
items.answer: Emergency aid responds to disasters with food, shelter and medicine; development aid funds long-term improvements in health, education and infrastructure.
items.markingKey: Emergency aid responds to disasters with food, shelter and medicine; development aid funds long-term improvements in health, education and infrastructure. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A class brainstorm on strategies to reduce inequality: aid, debt relief, microfinance and fair trade produced the question "Does aid work?" Explain why it needs refining, then suggest an improved research question and justify your change.
items.answer: Weakness: it is too broad and closed Improved: "How far did debt relief under the HIPC Initiative improve access to primary education in Tanzania between 2000 and 2010?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is too broad and closed); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How far did debt relief under the HIPC Initiative improve access to primary education in Tanzania between 2000 and 2010?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Mohammed argues that "Aid is the most effective strategy for reducing global inequality." Rafael disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality.
items.markingKey: Mohammed: aid has funded vaccination campaigns that saved millions of lives. Rafael: trade, investment and remittances are much larger flows. Judgement (1-2 marks): Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Aid is the most effective strategy for reducing global inequality."
items.answer: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: aid has funded vaccination campaigns that saved millions of lives; it supports health and education in the poorest countries. Arguments against: trade, investment and remittances are much larger flows; aid can create dependency and be poorly targeted. Supported judgement: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality.

items.stem: Explain why aid is controversial.
items.answer: Supporters say it saves lives and builds services; critics argue it can create dependency, support corrupt governments and serve donor interests.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Supporters say it saves lives and builds services; critics argue it can create dependency, support corrupt governments and serve donor interests. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Describe the research methods you would use to answer "How far did debt relief under the HIPC Initiative improve access to primary education in Tanzania between 2000 and 2010?", naming specific sources and explaining why each is appropriate.
items.answer: Use UNESCO enrolment data, government budgets and two studies; compare before and after; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Use UNESCO enrolment data, government budgets and two studies; compare before and after; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Aid is the most effective strategy for reducing global inequality."
items.answer: Thesis: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: aid has funded vaccination campaigns that saved millions of lives; it supports health and education in the poorest countries. Counter-arguments: trade, investment and remittances are much larger flows; aid can create dependency and be poorly targeted. Thesis/conclusion: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 or 100 (one person has all income)"?
items.answer: Gini coefficient
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of Gini coefficient.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A country experiencing rapid economic growth and industrialisation, such as India, Brazil or Indonesia"?
items.answer: emerging economy
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of emerging economy.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "dependency theory".
items.answer: The theory that poorer countries remain underdeveloped because of exploitative economic relationships with richer countries
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the theory that poorer countries remain underdeveloped because of exploitative economic relationships with richer countries. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: "Rich countries give most of their national income as aid." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Most give well under 1% of GNI; the average for OECD donors was about 0.37% in 2023.
items.markingKey: Most give well under 1% of GNI; the average for OECD donors was about 0.37% in 2023. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "A high GDP per capita means everyone in a country is well off." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It is an average; high inequality, as in some oil-rich states, can leave many people poor.
items.markingKey: It is an average; high inequality, as in some oil-rich states, can leave many people poor. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "A country's place on the Brandt line never changes." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: The line was a 1980 snapshot; countries have moved between income groups since.
items.markingKey: The line was a 1980 snapshot; countries have moved between income groups since. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why reliance on primary commodities can hinder development.
items.answer: Commodity prices are volatile and often fall relative to manufactured goods, and raw materials add little value or employment.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Commodity prices are volatile and often fall relative to manufactured goods, and raw materials add little value or employment. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "Aid always reaches the poorest people." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Aid can be lost to corruption, administrative costs or spent on donor priorities.
items.markingKey: Aid can be lost to corruption, administrative costs or spent on donor priorities. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between social indicators and economic indicators.
items.answer: Economic indicators measure income and production, such as GDP per capita; social indicators measure quality of life, such as life expectancy, literacy and infant mortality.
items.markingKey: Economic indicators measure income and production, such as GDP per capita; social indicators measure quality of life, such as life expectancy, literacy and infant mortality. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why GDP per capita is a limited measure of development.
items.answer: It is an average that hides inequality, ignores the informal and unpaid economy, says nothing about health, education, freedom or the environment, and is affected by exchange rates unless PPP is used.

items.stem: With reference to South Korea, explain how it illustrates closing the development gap.
items.answer: GDP per capita rose from under US$ 200 in 1960 to over US$ 33,000 by 2023 through export-led growth, education and state-guided industrial policy. It shows a country moving from "South" to high income within two generations.
items.markingKey: Context (GDP per capita rose from under US$ 200 in 1960 to over US$ 33,000 by 2023 through export-led growth, education and state-guided industrial policy.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: it shows a country moving from "South" to high income within two generations. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to closing the development gap.

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Daron Acemoglu and James A. Robinson, Why Nations Fail, New York, 2012

The authors argued that nations fail mainly because of "extractive" political and economic institutions that concentrate power and wealth in a narrow elite, while nations prosper when they have "inclusive" institutions that give broad groups a stake in the economy.

Outline the main argument or view that Source A presents, quoting or referring to the source.
items.answer: Inclusive institutions are the main cause of prosperity.
items.markingKey: Inclusive institutions are the main cause of prosperity. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Dambisa Moyo, Dead Aid: Why Aid Is Not Working and How There Is Another Way for Africa, London, 2009

The author argued that large aid flows to African governments had fostered dependency, encouraged corruption and slowed growth, and proposed phasing out aid over five years in favour of trade, investment and access to capital markets.

How reliable is Source A for someone researching strategies to reduce inequality: aid, debt relief, microfinance and fair trade? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Dambisa Moyo, Dead Aid: Why Aid Is Not Working and How There Is Another Way for Africa, London, 2009. Purpose: to challenge the consensus in favour of aid. Value: It is a provocative view from an African economist with financial experience. Limitation: Critics argue it focuses on government-to-government aid and ignores successes in health aid.
items.markingKey: Origin: Paraphrase of Dambisa Moyo, Dead Aid: Why Aid Is Not Working and How There Is Another Way for Africa, London, 2009. Purpose: to challenge the consensus in favour of aid. Value: It is a provocative view from an African economist with financial experience. Limitation: Critics argue it focuses on government-to-government aid and ignores successes in health aid. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". MYP I&S criterion D (year 5), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly discusses concepts, issues, models and theories, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, effectively analyses and evaluates a wide range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and thoroughly interprets a range of perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate; 1-2 limited.

items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "The HDI is the best measure of development."
items.answer: The HDI is more rounded than GDP per capita, but a range of indicators, including the inequality-adjusted HDI and MPI, gives a fuller picture.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: it combines income with health and education; it is simple and comparable across countries. Arguments against: it ignores inequality, freedom, gender and the environment; composite indices can hide important differences. Supported judgement: The HDI is more rounded than GDP per capita, but a range of indicators, including the inequality-adjusted HDI and MPI, gives a fuller picture.

items.stem: Plan an extended response to the question: "The Brandt line is no longer useful for understanding global development." To what extent do you agree? Give a thesis, two arguments with specific evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion.
items.answer: Thesis: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: NICs and emerging economies have blurred the divide; income groups and HDI give more nuance. Counter-arguments: it still captures a broad historical and power divide in global institutions; many "South" countries share colonial histories and interests. Thesis/conclusion: The Brandt line is too simple as a map of income today, but the idea of a Global South remains useful for understanding shared histories and political interests. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Estimates: Indonesia – GDP US$ 1,370 bn, population 278 m (2023); China – GDP US$ 17,790 bn, population 1,410 m (2023). Calculate GDP per capita for both, the ratio between them, and explain one limitation of GDP per capita as a measure of development.
items.answer: Indonesia: US$ 4,928; China: US$ 12,617; ratio ≈ 2.6
items.markingKey: Indonesia US$ 4,928 (A1); China US$ 12,617 (A1); China ≈ 2.6 × Indonesia (A1). Limitation (2): an average hides inequality; ignores informal work, unpaid work and quality of life; not adjusted for cost of living unless PPP is used.

items.stem: Sweden: GNI about US$ 650 billion; aid 0.91% of GNI (approx., OECD, 2023). Calculate its aid, the amount it would give at the UN 0.7% target, and the difference. Evaluate whether meeting the target would be the best way for it to reduce global inequality.
items.answer: aid US$ 5.9 bn; target US$ 4.5 bn; difference US$ -1.4 bn
items.markingKey: Aid 0.91% × 650 = 5.9 (A1); target 0.7% × 650 = 4.5 (A1); difference -1.4 bn (A1; negative means it already exceeds the target). Evaluation (3): quality and targeting of aid matter as much as quantity; trade rules, debt relief, tax justice and climate finance also matter.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "GDP per capita".
items.answer: The total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year divided by its population
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year divided by its population. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "development gap".
items.answer: The difference in levels of development between the richest and poorest countries
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the difference in levels of development between the richest and poorest countries. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which country is often cited as escaping the resource curse through good governance of diamond revenues?
items.answer: Botswana
items.markingKey: Botswana. It grew rapidly after independence.

items.stem: Distinguish between bottom-up development and top-down development.
items.answer: Top-down projects are planned by governments or agencies, often large-scale like dams; bottom-up projects are led by local communities, often small-scale like wells.
items.markingKey: Top-down projects are planned by governments or agencies, often large-scale like dams; bottom-up projects are led by local communities, often small-scale like wells. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims: "The HDI measures happiness." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It measures health, education and income; happiness is measured separately, for example in the World Happiness Report.
items.markingKey: It measures health, education and income; happiness is measured separately, for example in the World Happiness Report. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the development gap within countries and the development gap between countries.
items.answer: Between countries it compares national averages; within countries it compares regions, cities and rural areas or social groups.
items.markingKey: Between countries it compares national averages; within countries it compares regions, cities and rural areas or social groups. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims: "All countries must follow the same path to develop." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Countries have developed in different ways; Rostow's model is criticised for assuming one Western path.
items.markingKey: Countries have developed in different ways; Rostow's model is criticised for assuming one Western path. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "Aid always reaches the poorest people." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Aid can be lost to corruption, administrative costs or spent on donor priorities.
items.markingKey: Aid can be lost to corruption, administrative costs or spent on donor priorities. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "Development is only about money." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Following Sen, development includes freedoms, health, education, political rights and environmental quality.
items.markingKey: Following Sen, development includes freedoms, health, education, political rights and environmental quality. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source A – Commission report (paraphrased): Paraphrase of the Independent Commission on International Development Issues (chair Willy Brandt), North–South: A Programme for Survival, 1980

The report argued that the North and the South had a mutual interest in reducing poverty and inequality: a more prosperous South would provide markets and stability for the North. It called for large transfers of resources, reform of international institutions and an end to protectionism.

Identify two points that Source A makes about global patterns of development: the Brandt line and the development gap, using evidence from the source.
items.answer: North and South share an interest in reducing global inequality.
items.markingKey: North and South share an interest in reducing global inequality. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [2]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem: Kenji argues that "Historical factors such as colonialism are the most important cause of uneven development today." Kwame disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Colonial history shaped starting conditions, but post-independence choices, institutions and global economics explain much of today's variation.
items.markingKey: Kenji: colonial economic structures and borders persist. Kwame: many former colonies such as South Korea and Singapore developed rapidly. Judgement (1-2 marks): Colonial history shaped starting conditions, but post-independence choices, institutions and global economics explain much of today's variation.

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Dambisa Moyo, Dead Aid: Why Aid Is Not Working and How There Is Another Way for Africa, London, 2009

The author argued that large aid flows to African governments had fostered dependency, encouraged corruption and slowed growth, and proposed phasing out aid over five years in favour of trade, investment and access to capital markets.

According to Source A, what can we learn about strategies to reduce inequality: aid, debt relief, microfinance and fair trade? Support your answer with details from the source.
items.answer: Aid has harmed African development and should be replaced by market-based finance.
items.markingKey: Aid has harmed African development and should be replaced by market-based finance. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem: In 2023 Germany had a GDP of about US$ 4,460 billion and a population of about 84.5 million. Calculate its GDP per capita.
items.answer: about US$ 52,781
items.markingKey: GDP ÷ population = 4,460 × 10⁹ ÷ (84.5 × 10⁶) = US$ 52,781 (M1 A1). Watch the units (billions vs millions).

items.stem: Ghana's GDP per capita went from 183 US$ in 1960 to 2,260 US$ in 2023. Which is the percentage change?
Which of the following is the most clear and focused research question for an investigation into the causes of uneven development: physical, historical, economic and political factors?
options: Which country is the most developed?
How far does governance explain the different development paths of Botswana and Zimbabwe since 1980?
items.answer: How far does governance explain the different development paths of Botswana and Zimbabwe since 1980?
items.markingKey: B. It is open, has a clear scope (place/period/group) and can be answered with evidence; the others are too broad, closed or off-topic.

items.stem: Briefly describe WaterAid in Ethiopia and explain what it reveals about bottom-up development.
items.answer: WaterAid works with local partners to build hand-dug wells and train communities to maintain them. Local involvement makes projects more sustainable.
items.markingKey: Context (WaterAid works with local partners to build hand-dug wells and train communities to maintain them.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: local involvement makes projects more sustainable. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to bottom-up development.

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Amartya Sen, Development as Freedom, Oxford, 1999

The author argued that development should be seen as a process of expanding the real freedoms that people enjoy, such as freedom from hunger, disease and illiteracy, and political freedom, rather than only as growth in income.

Using Source A and your own knowledge, evaluate the claim that "The HDI is the best measure of development."
items.answer: The HDI is more rounded than GDP per capita, but a range of indicators, including the inequality-adjusted HDI and MPI, gives a fuller picture.
items.markingKey: From the source: Development means expanding people's freedoms and capabilities. Own knowledge for: it combines income with health and education; it is simple and comparable across countries. Own knowledge against: it ignores inequality, freedom, gender and the environment; composite indices can hide important differences. Judgement: The HDI is more rounded than GDP per capita, but a range of indicators, including the inequality-adjusted HDI and MPI, gives a fuller picture. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 5), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly discusses concepts, issues, models and theories, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, effectively analyses and evaluates a wide range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and thoroughly interprets a range of perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate; 1-2 limited.

items.stem: A class brainstorm on global patterns of development: the Brandt line and the development gap produced the question "Why are some countries poor?" Explain why it needs refining, then suggest an improved research question and justify your change.
items.answer: Weakness: it is too broad Improved: "How has the development gap between South Korea and Ghana changed since 1960, and why?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is too broad); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How has the development gap between South Korea and Ghana changed since 1960, and why?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Historical factors such as colonialism are the most important cause of uneven development today."
items.answer: Thesis: Colonial history shaped starting conditions, but post-independence choices, institutions and global economics explain much of today's variation.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: colonial economic structures and borders persist; dependency on commodity exports continues. Counter-arguments: many former colonies such as South Korea and Singapore developed rapidly; governance, conflict and policy since independence matter greatly. Thesis/conclusion: Colonial history shaped starting conditions, but post-independence choices, institutions and global economics explain much of today's variation. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Dambisa Moyo, Dead Aid: Why Aid Is Not Working and How There Is Another Way for Africa, London, 2009

The author argued that large aid flows to African governments had fostered dependency, encouraged corruption and slowed growth, and proposed phasing out aid over five years in favour of trade, investment and access to capital markets.

"Aid is the most effective strategy for reducing global inequality." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?
items.answer: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality.
items.markingKey: From the source: Aid has harmed African development and should be replaced by market-based finance. Own knowledge for: aid has funded vaccination campaigns that saved millions of lives; it supports health and education in the poorest countries. Own knowledge against: trade, investment and remittances are much larger flows; aid can create dependency and be poorly targeted. Judgement: Aid is important for health and emergencies, but trade, investment, debt relief and good governance are more powerful long-term drivers of reducing inequality. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 5), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly discusses concepts, issues, models and theories, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, effectively analyses and evaluates a wide range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and thoroughly interprets a range of perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate; 1-2 limited.
